text:
12\. Family participation can become a powerful therapeutic intervention. The presentation's central innovation is involving relatives in medication planning, glucose monitoring and emergency decisions. Family agreement before fasting may improve adherence to safety recommendations and reduce delays in treatment.

13\. Religious rituals can be converted into monitoring opportunities. Glucose testing can be linked to familiar Chhath milestones such as Kharna, Sandhya Arghya and Usha Arghya. This culturally integrated approach may improve acceptance of monitoring, although its effectiveness requires formal evaluation.

14\. The post-fast meal deserves as much attention as the fast itself. Traditional prasad may contain concentrated carbohydrates from jaggery, sugar, rice flour and wheat flour. Portion control, gradual rehydration and appropriate medication resumption can help prevent postprandial hyperglycaemia and gastrointestinal discomfort.

15\. The physician's role is not simply to prohibit fasting but to reduce preventable harm. Culturally sensitive counselling, shared decision-making, individualized medication adjustments and an agreed emergency plan can improve engagement. However, patients at substantial medical risk should be clearly advised against prolonged dry fasting.

 Five particularly important scientific qualifications

The presentation offers a compelling educational framework, but several recommendations should not be interpreted as universally validated protocols.

1\. The 36-hour danger-zone diagram is conceptual. It does not establish a scientifically validated time-dependent decline in hydration or glucose reserves for every patient.

2\. Medication withdrawal schedules are not universal. The suggested 48-hour SGLT2 inhibitor hold and fixed restart schedules for sulfonylureas or diuretics require individualized assessment. SGLT2 inhibitor withholding may need to begin earlier in selected high-risk situations.

3\. A glucose level of 70–300 mg/dL is not automatically a safe fasting zone. Significant dehydration, hypotension and euglycaemic DKA can occur within that range.

4\. Stopping antihypertensive treatment indiscriminately can be harmful. Beta-blockers, clonidine and other medications may cause withdrawal-related complications. Adjustments should consider their indications and cardiovascular risks.

5\. Claims of 100% monitoring adherence through religious integration are illustrative, not proven outcomes. The presentation is a clinical teaching narrative, not a controlled intervention study.

CME INDIA — Final clinical message

“The greatest clinical innovation is not always a new drug. Sometimes it is the ability to integrate medical science with a patient's deeply held beliefs—without compromising safety.”

The key physician-level takeaway is that 36-hour Nirjala fasting in patients with diabetes and hypertension requires a distinct risk-assessment and medication-management strategy, rather than routine advice borrowed from Ramadan or intermittent-fasting guidelines.

Source: Green Tea with CME INDIA, Chhath episode, 12 November 2026. The pearls are derived from the presentation.

text:
During the Char Dham Yatra in the Himalayas, a wealthy devotee named Vikram Singh (from a traditional Hindu family in Rajasthan) was staying in a luxurious camp tent near the mountain base. 

On one evening he felt a strange restlessness in his heart and decided to go for a solitary walk into the hills, leaving his staff behind and taking only his phone.

Night had fallen. After walking some distance he saw an old sadhu sitting alone on a rock.

The sadhu looked at him and asked calmly:  
“Have you brought the pure vegetarian food for me?”

Vikram was surprised. “Were you waiting for someone to bring food? Did you order from somewhere?”

The sadhu replied with complete certainty:  
“I asked Bhagwan. He is the master of all kitchens and all cooks. I have not eaten since afternoon. I asked Him for a proper vegetarian meal, and I am simply waiting for whoever He sends.”

Vikram was astonished that this elderly man was sitting alone in a remote, deserted place at night, fully trusting that food would arrive. He decided to fulfil the request. He contacted the camp organiser and asked for a large, excellent pure vegetarian thali (paneer sabzi, dal, seasonal vegetables, puri/roti, rice and salad).

Soon a worker arrived with the thali. Vikram placed it in front of the sadhu.

The old man exclaimed with joy:  
“Har Har Mahadev! Jai Shri Krishna!”

He took Bhagwan’s name and began eating with great relish, as if he had been hungry for days.

When he finished, he said:  
“O Parmatma, now I also need a cup of fresh tulsi-adrak chai.”

Vikram was even more amazed. In that isolated spot, with no shops or houses nearby, the sadhu was now asking for tulsi tea.

The sadhu looked at him and asked:  
“Do you want the leftover food?”

“No, thank you,” Vikram replied.

The sadhu gathered the remaining food and gave it to the first few pilgrims who happened to pass by.

A short while later one of them returned, holding a cup of hot tulsi-adrak chai.

He said to the sadhu:  
“Please accept this. Just as we accepted the food from you, please accept this chai.”

The sadhu replied:  
“Can you also bring a cup for this gentleman sitting with me? Bhagwan sent him to bring the food to me and to you.”

After that the old sadhu lay down to rest.

Vikram heard him softly praying:  
“O Bhagwan, the night is still warm. Please send a cool breeze so I can sleep peacefully.”

Within a short time a cool mountain breeze began to blow.

Tears came to Vikram’s eyes and he spontaneously said:  
“Har Har Mahadev! Om Namah Shivaya!”

He asked the sadhu:  
“Baba, who are you?”

The sadhu answered simply:  
“I am just an ordinary servant of Bhagwan, like you. Now let me sleep. Tomorrow is a long day of the yatra. If you keep talking I will pray that you also get tired and leave.”

Vikram felt a deep sense of awe and quietly returned to his tent.

Later he told his guru about the encounter. The guru wished to meet the man, so they went back to the same spot. The sadhu was no longer lying down; he was walking.

Vikram called out:  
“Baba, where are you going?”

“It is time for the morning bath and prayers. I am going to the stream.”

Vikram asked whether the sadhu knew who he was and who the accompanying guru was.

The sadhu replied with complete simplicity:  
“Yes. Both of you are also Bhagwan’s servants, just like me.”

Even after Vikram introduced himself and the guru, the sadhu remained unimpressed and repeated the same words. When invited to complete the remaining yatra with them in comfort, he declined, saying he preferred to do his pilgrimage in his own simple way.

In the end Vikram offered his personal number and said the sadhu could call anytime if he needed anything. The old man simply smiled and walked on, fully absorbed in his own path.

Such is the power of pure shraddha and complete trust in Bhagwan. Some devotees place their needs before the Lord before they ever place them before people. They know the Giver is greater than any means He uses.

text:
*Karthika Shuddha Chavithi - Nagula Chavithi*

The fourth day (Chaturthi) of the bright fortnight in the month of Karthika is known as 'Nagula Chavithi'. On this day, snakes (Nagas) are worshipped. Since it is not practical to bring snakes into one's home, people visit the places where snakes reside—typically their burrows (anthills)—to offer worship. Nagula Chavithi is observed by people across all social strata. On this day, after a ritual bath, devotees go to an anthill and offer items associated with snakes, such as cow's milk, *chimmili* (a mixture of sesame seeds and jaggery), and *chalimidi* (a preparation of rice flour and jaggery); some even offer eggs. They circumambulate the anthill, often accompanied by their children, offer their salutations, and then return home. When worshipping the snake, it is revered as a deity. Instead of reciting complex Sanskrit *shlokas* (hymns), devotees offer a simple, heartfelt prayer while standing before the anthill. They say: "O Naganna (Serpent Deity), protect me and my lineage. Protect my home, my parents, and my loved ones. If I happen to step on your hood, do not consider me an enemy; if I step on your midsection, consider me one of your own; and if I step on your tail, please simply move away. Accept these offerings, and in return, bless us with children."
Lord Subrahmanya (Kartikeya) is considered the deity associated with the Nagas and is also the bestower of progeny. For this reason, elders often suggest that the reproductive elements (sperm cells) within the male seed move in a serpentine, slithering manner. Among the names of Subrahmanya, there is one that goes, "Vamshavriddhi Karakaya Namah" (Salutations to the One who causes the lineage to flourish). He is the bestower of progeny and ensures the continuity of a lineage. For this reason, people regard the serpent as a manifestation of Subrahmanya; they visit the serpent’s burrow (anthill) and offer milk.

text:
In this video, Donald Trump was in Corinth, Mississippi, to help Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith keep her seat. Scott Colom, the Democrat running to take it, went to the same rally and started talking to people waiting in line.

“What matters to you as a veteran right now?” he asked one man. The man brought up gun rights. Others talked about the price of gas and the war in Iran. 

Now Colom has defeated Hyde-Smith, and I keep coming back to this clip. Here was a man running for the U.S. Senate who walked up to people waiting to cheer for his opponent and gave them the first word.

Watching him, I thought of Mark Antony in Shakespeare’s Julius Caesar. By the time Antony rose to speak, Brutus had already persuaded the crowd that Caesar had to die. Caesar was ambitious, Brutus told them, and killing him had saved Rome. One man warned that Antony had better say nothing against Brutus. Another called Caesar a tyrant. This was the crowd Antony had to win over.

“Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears,” he began. 

The first word matters. He called them friends. Then he repeated the argument they had just cheered. “The noble Brutus hath told you Caesar was ambitious.” 

Only then did Antony ask them to think about something they had seen with their own eyes. Caesar had been offered a crown three times and had refused it each time. “Was this ambition?”

Go back to that line in Corinth and watch what Colom does. He could have opened with everything he thought Cindy Hyde-Smith had gotten wrong. Instead, he asked a veteran what mattered to him and let the man answer in his own words. You can hear gun rights, gas prices and the war come up because Colom gave people room to tell him what had brought them there and what was on their minds.

Antony understood what his audience had already been persuaded to believe. Colom went to Corinth to find out what his audience cared about. I think that Ian what makes this clip worth watching. Before he asked those voters to give him a hearing, he gave them one.

May the day break

# From the Jim Crow Era to the U.S. Senate: Scott Colom’s Historic Victory Marks a New Chapter in Mississippi’s 150-Year Struggle for Equality

A powerful reminder of America's long journey from slavery, racial segregation, and voter suppression toward civil rights, equal opportunity, and political representation.

For more than 150 years, generations of African Americans have fought courageously to overcome the barriers of discrimination and injustice. Their sacrifices helped transform American democracy and opened doors that were once denied to millions.

Scott Colom's historic achievement symbolizes the progress made since the Jim Crow era and the continuing importance of protecting voting rights, strengthening democracy, and ensuring that every American has an opportunity to serve and lead.

This moment carries a message far beyond Mississippi. It offers inspiration to African Americans, immigrant communities, and future generations who believe in the American promise of freedom, equality, justice, and opportunity.

It also reminds us that the struggle for equality was never simply about winning elections. It was about securing human dignity, overcoming generations of injustice, and ensuring that the principles enshrined in the United States Constitution apply equally to every citizen, regardless of race, background, or origin.

**History reminds us where we came from. Democracy gives us the power to shape where we go next.**

May this historic moment inspire continued progress toward a more inclusive, just, and united America.

**Congratulations to Scott Colom on this historic milestone!**

May the sacrifices of past generations continue to inspire future leaders and strengthen the enduring promise of American democracy.

text:
THE 67 BALLOTS THAT PROTECTED DEMOCRACY: WHY EVERY VOTE MUST COUNT

What happens when the right to vote is protected by law, but political interests demand that legally cast ballots be discarded? Mississippi offers an important lesson.

SOURCE ATTRIBUTION

Marc Elias, Founder of Democracy Docket. Commentary on the Mississippi Senate election and the Supreme Court's decision in Watson v. Republican National Committee.

Original newsletter: Democracy Docket, November 11, 2026. A direct article URL was not included in the supplied email.

THE DEMOCRATIC SIGNIFICANCE OF 67 BALLOTS

Sometimes, democracy turns on a number that looks insignificant.

In Hinds County, Mississippi, election officials received, processed and counted 67 absentee ballots during the five business days following Election Day. Those ballots increased Scott Colom's margin by a net 58 votes.

The voters had done everything required of them. They had completed and mailed their ballots on time. The delay was caused by postal delivery, not by any failure on their part.

Yet those 67 votes could have been discarded.

And that is precisely what makes this story so important.

Democracy is not merely about holding elections. It is about ensuring that every eligible citizen can exercise the right to vote and that every legally cast ballot receives equal consideration.

THE LAW, THE COURTS AND THE RIGHT TO VOTE

In January 2024, the Republican National Committee sued Mississippi to invalidate its law permitting absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted if received within five business days.

The political argument was revealing. The RNC's own legal filing acknowledged that these late-arriving ballots disproportionately favoured Democrats.

The case eventually reached the US Supreme Court. In June 2026, the Court ruled 5–4 in Watson v. Republican National Committee that federal election-day statutes do not prohibit states from counting ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward within the period permitted by state law.

Justice Amy Coney Barrett, writing for the majority, reaffirmed that states retain primary responsibility for the mechanics of congressional elections.

This judgment protected more than Mississippi's election law. It protected the voting rights of citizens who should never be punished for postal delays beyond their control. LII / Legal Information Institute +1

WHEN VOTING RIGHTS BECOME A POLITICAL BATTLEGROUND

The deeper concern is the growing use of litigation to restrict access to the ballot.

When political organisations challenge legally established voting procedures, the consequences extend beyond party competition. They affect citizens' ability to participate equally in democracy.

The concern becomes even more serious when racial demographics overlap significantly with partisan voting patterns.

Hinds County is more than 70% Black. Excluding valid absentee ballots there would have disproportionately affected a community whose participation is essential to representative democracy.

Voting rights cannot depend on whether the ballots favour Democrats or Republicans. The same standards must apply regardless of political consequences.

67 BALLOTS, 58 VOTES AND 4,669 VOTES

Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by 4,669 votes, according to the Associated Press's November 11 projection.

The 67 absentee ballots in Hinds County contributed a net 58 votes to his margin. They did not independently decide the election, but they demonstrate why every legally cast ballot matters.

Colom's victory is historic: he becomes Mississippi's first Black US senator since Reconstruction. AP News +2

THE LESSON FOR DEMOCRACIES EVERYWHERE

Democracy is not simply the right to cast a ballot. It is the right to have that ballot counted under fair, transparent and consistently applied rules.

A voter who follows the law must not lose their voice because a postal service is slow. Nor should election laws be manipulated to benefit one political party at the expense of another.

The integrity of elections rests on equal voting rights, independent institutions, judicial accountability and public confidence.

The real test of democracy is not whether a political party wins. It is whether the system protects the rights of citizens even when their votes produce an outcome that those in power dislike.

A ballot is not a political favour. It is a democratic right. Every valid vote must count.

Democracy cannot survive when electoral rules become weapons of political exclusion.

#DimaagiNaxal #Resistance #UnitedResistance

Verification note: The Supreme Court judgment and the reported election result are independently corroborated by the cited sources.

The courage and sacrifice of those who fought for Latvia’s freedom and independence were remembered in Colorado Springs as 🇱🇻Ambassador to 🇺🇸 Elita Kuzma, together with Honorary Consul Aivars Ziediņš, marked Lāčplēsis Day with the local Latvian community. 

The visit began at the Penrose Public Library, where the Ambassador explored historical archives highlighting the legacy of Latvians in Colorado Springs. 

At the Freedom Fountain, Ambassador Kuzma paid tribute to Latvia’s defenders. Built thanks to donations from the Latvian community, the fountain features an abstract form inspired by the kokle, a traditional Latvian musical instrument, and stars referencing Latvia’s coat of arms. Presented as a gift to the people of Colorado Springs in gratitude for the freedom and refuge offered to Latvian refugees, the fountain stands as a symbol of hope for those who cherish freedom and the right to self-determination. 

The commemoration continued at Evergreen Cemetery, where flowers were placed at the graves of Edvīns Šneiders and Aleksandrs Žīgurs, recipients of Lāčplēsis Military Order.

Sincere gratitude to the Latvian community in Colorado Springs for preserving our history, honoring our heroes, and keeping Latvia’s spirit alive across generations.

text:
🧭 MOUNT HILLABY | TRAVEL ESSENTIALS
📍 Getting There

Located in Saint Andrew, Mount Hillaby is best reached by rental car or a prearranged local driver. Follow the narrow, winding road through Hillaby village toward the summit. A local guide can simplify navigation.

🗺️ What to Explore

The main attraction is the sweeping countryside panorama rather than a demanding climb. A short path near the road's end leads to the summit survey marker. Enjoy views across the Scotland District, with the eastern and northern coastlines visible in clear weather. Combine the visit with Bathsheba for a contrasting Atlantic coastal experience.

⏱️ Time Needed

Allow 30–60 minutes for the viewpoint and short walk, excluding travel. A half-day outing provides more flexibility for exploring the surrounding countryside.

🌤️ When to Visit

December–May generally offers drier conditions. Early mornings can bring atmospheric mist, although clearer views may emerge later as it lifts.

💰 Costs & Booking

The summit is generally described as freely accessible. Budget separately for transportation or a guided excursion, and confirm current arrangements before travelling.

text:
NEW FINDING OF THE DAY | THE DIVINE WARDROBE OF INDIA

When Poetry Becomes a Garment: The Sacred Khandua of Lord Jagannath

Did you know that the verses of the 12th-century Sanskrit masterpiece Geeta Govinda are woven into silk textiles offered to Lord Jagannath in Puri, Odisha?

This extraordinary textile is known as Khandua Pata.

Crafted using Odisha’s traditional Bandha (Ikat) technique, Khandua is not just a piece of silk. It represents a beautiful confluence of literature, devotion and craftsmanship.

The fascinating part is that the patterns and verses are created by resist-dyeing the yarn before it reaches the loom. The poetry is not printed onto the fabric; it is woven into its very structure.

Traditionally associated with the weaving communities of Nuapatna and Maniabandha, this textile carries a legacy that connects generations of artisans with the sacred rituals of the Jagannath Temple.

Think about it for a moment:

A poem written in devotion, transformed into a textile, and offered as a garment to the divine.

Perhaps this is one of the most beautiful expressions of India’s textile heritage — where weaving transcends craftsmanship and becomes an act of worship.

For me, this discovery reinforces a thought: India’s textiles were never merely about what we wore. They were also about what we believed, celebrated and offered.

When devotion finds its way to the loom, even fabric becomes sacred.

#NewFindingOfTheDay #KhanduaPata #Jagannath #OdishaTextiles #IndianHandloom #GeetaGovinda #Shubhvastram #TextileHeritage

text:
Jyotisha Diaries
Rahu in Makara and Ketu in Karka: Transit and Remedies
December 5, 2026 – June 24, 2028

Rahu wants the crown. Saturn asks for the work. Which one is running your chart?

After nearly 18 years, Rahu is transiting into Makara (Capricorn) and Ketu into Karka (Cancer).

Rahu and Ketu are the shadowy planets called the lunar nodes. They are always opposite each other and move backwards (retrogression).

Rahu is depicted as a head, full of desires, ambition, money and the greater acquisition.

Ketu, on the other hand, is headless. He represents detachment, introspection, past karmas and spiritual liberation.

Rahu in Capricorn
Rahu's ingress into Capricorn, lorded by Saturn, the planet of duty, karma and responsibility.
Rahu's transit here heightens professional ambition for greater authority, recognition, wealth and worldly success, as Capricorn is the natural tenth house of career in the zodiac.
Rahu's desire in this sign conflicts with Saturn's lesson: pursue success through hard work, patience and ethical ways.

Ketu in Karka
Karka is the natural fourth house of the zodiac, lorded by Chandra (Moon). The Moon is the significator of mind, mother, nurturing figures and domestic harmony.
Ketu's transit through Karka brings a certain detachment to these aspects of life.
The spiritual lesson is not to abandon everything but to strive for emotional balance.

Traditional Remedies: 
Rahu
1Worship Goddess Durga. Chant ॐ दुं दुर्गायै नमः, preferably 108 times, according to your capacity. Four malas is the usual practice.
2Chant ॐ राहवे नमः 108 times on Saturday if you cannot do it daily. Three malas.
3Light a sesame-oil diya on Saturdays. Sesame oil may also be offered at a Shani temple.
4Donate black sesame seeds or food to the needy, particularly on Saturdays.
5Worship Lord Shiva. Offer Jalabhisheka to the Shivlinga, chanting ॐ नमः शिवाय।

Ketu
1Worship Ganpati, the remover of obstacles.
2Chant ॐ गजवक्त्राय नमः, 108 times or three malas.
3Pray to Lord Shiva for spiritual progress.
4Pray for your mother's well-being and try to keep domestic peace.
5Make food donations to needy families.

Additional voluntary sankalpas include visiting Bhimashankar to perform Shiva worship or offer charity there. The mantras are:
ॐ नमः शिवाय।
ॐ भीमशंकराय नमः।
Bhimashankar Jyotirlingam is associated with Capricorn.
Sapta Rishi Aarti at Kashi Vishwanath. 

The Sapta Rishi Aarti at Kashi Vishwanath honours Lord Shiva and the seven great Rishis.
Participation, whether in person or through a sankalpa, is beneficial, though it is not a mandatory remedy for Rahu–Ketu.

More importantly:
The results of Rahu–Ketu transits differ for every individual.

The lagna, Moon rashi, placement of Rahu and Ketu, their dispositors, and the running Mahadasha and Antardasha must all be considered.

For this transit, particular attention is given to Shani as the dispositor of Rahu and Chandra as the dispositor of Ketu.

The remedies are not substitutes for individual horoscope analysis.

Putting aside their national identities in the spirit of universal harmony, the foreign devotees stood patiently in long queues alongside Indian pilgrims. Dressed in traditional attire and carrying red hibiscus garlands, considered sacred to the deity, they offered special prayers to Goddess Tara, a manifestation of Mother Shakti, seeking an end to the devastating military conflict between their countries.

“We believe in Mother Shakti, Mahadev and the principles of karma-dharma,” said Ajay Giri, a Russian national travelling with the group. “We turned to Goddess Kali and Mother Tara because she is the ultimate symbol of cosmic power. Our unified prayer is simple: we want this destructive war to stop, and we hope for the return of peace and prosperity to both our countries.”

Pulak Chattopadhyay, secretary of the Tarapith Temple Committee, confirmed the visit, saying the international guests participated in the rituals just like other devotees. After the prayers, the temple authorities facilitated their visit and distributed sacred prasad among the group.

The shared prayer of the 15 foreign nationals at Tarapith stood out as a poignant appeal for peace, reflecting the festival’s message of light triumphing over darkness.

GRIFFIN CHARGED IN $51 MILLION MEDICARE FRAUD

Charlie Bernard Griffin III, president of First Coast Community Development in Jacksonville, was indicted on 31 counts on October 29 for his role in a scheme that billed Medicare, Medicaid, and private insurers more than $51 million for HIV prophylactic medications that patients never requested.

Prosecutors say marketers offered free cell phones to collect personal information from people who thought they were only signing up for a phone. That data was used to generate thousands of false prescriptions for expensive HIV drugs.

The pharmacy at the nonprofit filled the prescriptions and submitted more than 20,000 claims. Griffin allegedly received about $14.2 million from the proceeds. Co-conspirators including an accountant and a nurse who wrote the prescriptions have pleaded guilty.

If convicted on the healthcare fraud and money laundering counts, Griffin faces substantial prison time and forfeiture of millions, including bank accounts and real estate.

Sources: U.S. Department of Justice, Jacksonville Florida Times-Union, News4Jax

How many more free phone scams are hiding Medicare fraud?

text:
Tesla just launched a $350 Cybertruck RC racer as production winds down. Here's what you need to know.

Tesla added 22 new items to its online shop today, a holiday collection led by the Cybertruck RC Racer. The official Cybertruck account promoted it as "other Cybertruck news." It lands days after Elon Musk said Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas will wind down around mid-2027 to make room for the Cybercab robotaxi.

The RC racer has a quick-release polycarbonate body and an 11.1V 3S 3400mAh LiPo battery. Top speed is up to 37mph (60km/h) and run time is up to 20 minutes. Tesla China lists a 1:10 scale version with a brushless motor and 4WD for ¥1,769, about $245.

The cheaper items lean on both vehicles. Cybertruck and Cybercab pullback racers cost $35 each. There is also a 1:43 Cybercab diecast at $65 and a Tesla Action Figure 2.5 Factory Edition at $45.

Musk also said stopping the Cybertruck is not the smartest move from a profit-maximizing standpoint. He said there must be some room in the world for sentimentality.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis replied to a post about Tesla moving its HQ from Texas to Florida. He asked whether that would mean keeping the Cybertruck in production beyond next year. Rep. Carlos Giménez had invited Musk to relocate Tesla's headquarters.

Aftermarket firm Unplugged Performance has offered to take over the Cybertruck line. It says it would fund it with a consortium of investors, at no cost to Tesla's floor space or headcount. It also says it secured Cybertruck supply for first responders into 2027.

Meanwhile the Cybercab is spreading. Riders are posting first rides in Austin, and a display unit is at Starfield Mall in Anseong, South Korea, until Sunday.

Key numbers:
- 22 new Tesla shop items
- Cybertruck RC Racer: $350, up to 37mph, up to 20 minutes
- Pullback racers: $35 each
- 1:43 Cybercab diecast: $65
- Action Figure 2.5 Factory Edition: $45

The truck is ending in mid-2027, but the merch is just getting started.

text:
Tesla just stopped taking Cybertruck Premium AWD orders and raised the Cyberbeast price. Here's what you need to know.

Tesla has officially closed orders for the Cybertruck Premium AWD trim, per Sawyer Merritt on X. Dual Motor AWD orders were already closed. That leaves the Cyberbeast as the only Cybertruck trim you can order.

The Cyberbeast starting price rose $7,500, or 7.3%, to $109,990 from $102,490. Tesla also raised prices a few days earlier. Then Dual Motor AWD went to $82,490 from $74,990, Premium AWD went to $92,490 from $84,990, and Cyberbeast went from $99,990 to $102,490.

Wait times are growing fast. Cyberbeast delivery estimates across North America now show March to June 2027, up from January to March 2027. Just days ago they read December 2026 to January 2027. Merritt says Tesla will likely stop taking orders for all trims soon.

The backdrop is Tesla winding down the Cybertruck. Elon Musk says order rate far exceeds production rate. He says Tesla will build as many as it can before shutting the line in about 8 months, and will have to return deposits for many people. He says it is not a case of the Cybertruck being unprofitable. Reports say the floor space is being freed up for the Cybercab.

Reaction is split. Owners launched a petition against the discontinuation, and some compare it to GM's EV1. Others say the truck sold well in the $80,000 to $100,000 truck segment. They say the real miss was the promised $39,000 to $40,000 version. One post cites about 56,000 sold in 4 years, versus Musk's earlier hope of 250,000 a year. Tesla's Cybertruck account says the existing fleet stays on the road.

Key numbers:
- Cyberbeast: $109,990, up $7,500 (7.3%) from $102,490
- Premium AWD: $92,490, orders closed
- Dual Motor AWD: $82,490, orders closed
- Cyberbeast delivery estimate: March to June 2027
- Line shutdown: in about 8 months

For now, the Cyberbeast at $109,990 is the only Cybertruck Tesla will take an order for.

text:
I guess I should formally introduce myself. I will probably only do this one time. 

I’m Amy, the Architect & Founder of Life Giving Limbs (https://t.co/pP9wPjjkZ2).

We help children and Veterans in Florida and Texas who don’t qualify for a prosthesis through insurance. 100% of every donation goes directly to funding a limb for a child, Veteran, LEO, or First Responder. My husband and I cover all fees out of pocket. No admin fees, No paycheck from donations. Serving Veterans since 2021.

I work full-time in insurance (I see the gaps), so I can keep funding this and try to personally cover at least one child’s prosthetic each year. I’m also finishing a CACREP Master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, then moving into a Clinical Psychology doctorate. I’m building additional businesses that will expand the work, so that our warriors pay nothing for the proper care that they need and deserve. 

My goal is a new kind of mental health program built specifically for active duty & Veterans (really any individual who works in a high danger, high stress field). My program is purposefully designed to decrease the number of warriors who take their lives. Between 17 and 20 do every single day. Every day I spend on red tape is another 17–20 who can't, don't, or won’t wait. That thought is what drives me forward, because no matter what is happening in my own life, it doesn't compare to these 17-20 who will have the worst day of their lives, and so will everyone they know. Those ramifications continue to echo through multiple generations. 

I completed a double BA in Psychology and Military Resilience in two years instead of four, graduating with a 4.0 GPA, Summa Cum Laude on both degrees. I certified in Mental Health First Aid and as a Resilience Facilitator, (how I earned the nickname Nerd Supreme). My family military history stretches back 300 years from England to Jamestown forward and we lost men in WWII and Vietnam; still have men serving today. I was originally in NJROTC and planned on trying for OCS when I was hit by a car, ultimately making me medically ineligible to serve. Those losses shaped both my passions and my work.  I chose to serve this way instead. It's what I can offer and how I can continue our family legacy of service in and to our military.  Our family has fought, bled, and died for this country; and we gladly continue to do so today, plan to forever in fact, as long as this country stands, we will fight for it. 

Our warriors are the most valuable Americans we have. I’m building a bridge so that we can do better by them, because no one deserves it more than they do.

In what spare time I have (laughably little) I do paleontology, dig for seashell fossils that are millions of years old. It fascinates me because when it comes to seashells and stone fossils; well, man can't make those, only God can. To me it's tangible proof. I will never believe otherwise. 

I am also an award-winning photographer coming up on 500 photo awards, although not a single person even knows my name as it relates to photo, it's my own personal adventure, one that I rarely share with the world. My grandfather taught me how to take photos and develop my own film when I was 11. It's another of the family legacies I carry on. 

I am not only an advocate for positive mental health for all humans but I am also an advocate for lethal means safety and I am a 2A certified trainer, as well as a CRSO; so that I can not only train others on the importance of 2A, how to keep and use their 2A rights, but I am again formulating a new type of therapy program to help our warriors who return home with PTSD related to their job training tools. This is yet another family legacy I continue. @MossbergCorp @DanielDefense @onehorseusa reach out if you are interested in partnering with us on these efforts!

My entire program is designed specifically to decrease that statistic of 17-20. It is just going to take some time for me to get through the red tape. 

If I could say one thing, it is no matter what position life finds you in, you have the opportunity to assess that current posture and position and more adequately formulate a future response. No rash decisions, review the consequences and ramifications first, have someone you can go to as a sounding board for feedback or help. You never have to walk life alone, we as mankind do not live the human experience by ourselves. 

I am proof that here in America, if you want something bad enough, you can create a way to make it happen. Since my program doesn't exist anywhere out there, it is solely up to me to continue to be the advocate, architect, and foundation. Our 17-20 warriors aren't waiting, so I can't either, there's no time to waste.  

For those of you who followed me before I even told my story, I thank you for being here. I hope to meet many more of you as you walk through life as only you can.

text:
🇺🇸 🐡 America's Fastest Ocean Liner Sinks Off Florida to Anchor the World's Largest Artificial Reef

On Veterans Day, Okaloosa County scuttled the 990-foot SS United States 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin-Fort Walton Beach, converting the 1952 transatlantic speed record holder into a $13.5 million Gulf Coast reef after defeating eleventh-hour preservationist litigation.

Deployment operations commenced at 1:00 p.m. CST on November 11, 2026, moved forward 24 hours from Thursday to outrun approaching Gulf winds and heavy seas. Federal environmental and explosives regulations barred demolition charges, forcing contractors to scuttle the 47,000-ton hull through controlled flooding. Crews removed internal boiler-cooling tanks and opened seawater intake valves, while cutting 10-by-10-foot deck openings and stripping more than 400 portholes so air could escape and the 53,329-gross-register-ton vessel would settle upright at 30° 07.148' N, 86° 46.755' W. The site places the keel on sand 180 feet down, leaving the upper superstructure 55 to 60 feet beneath the surface for open-water divers while restricting deeper decks and sealed hazardous compartments to technical wreck specialists.

At 990 feet—108 feet longer than the RMS Titanic—the liner eclipses the 888-foot aircraft carrier USS Oriskany, sunk 12 nautical miles away off Pensacola in 2006, as the largest artificial reef on earth. Okaloosa County financed the $13.5 million acquisition, tow, and remediation through local tourist development taxes rather than federal grants, betting that a storied American hull will draw global dive charters and pelagic gamefish including tuna, marlin, amberjack, and red snapper. Marine researchers note that steel shipwrecks offer less immediate shelter density than perforated concrete reef balls, meaning the county's return hinges on diver tourism and long-term biological colonization rather than guaranteed fishery expansion.

Completed in 1952 by Newport News Shipbuilding under naval architect William Francis Gibbs, the SS United States embodied Cold War American industrial supremacy. Built with classified fireproofing, compartmentalized damage control, and 240,000-horsepower steam turbines, she was engineered to convert rapidly into a troopship capable of carrying an entire infantry division at sustained speeds above 35 knots. On her July 1952 maiden voyage, she crossed the Atlantic in three days, 10 hours, and 40 minutes, capturing the Blue Riband from the RMS Queen Mary by 10 hours—a passenger-liner speed record that remains unbroken after 74 years.

Jet aviation rendered transatlantic liners unprofitable by 1969, condemning the ship to 57 years of auctions, stripped interiors, and a nearly three-decade layup in South Philadelphia that consumed over $40 million in failed private redevelopment bids. After a 2024 pier eviction, Okaloosa County bought the vessel for roughly $1 million and towed her 1,800 nautical miles to Mobile, Alabama, in early 2025 for a year-long cleanup overseen by the EPA and Florida environmental regulators to strip wiring, plastics, fuel, and residual toxins. Crews preserved her 65-foot smokestacks and main mast for a land-based museum in Destin-Fort Walton Beach. On November 10, a federal judge rejected an eleventh-hour restraining order from the SS United States Preservation Foundation alleging hexavalent chromium risks and historic-preservation lapses, clearing the final legal obstacle before the hull slipped beneath the Gulf. https://t.co/bzyED5XkM2

Iran has not issued formal, enacted state bounties covering President Trump’s entire cabinet. Reported threats and claimed rewards have focused primarily on Trump himself, with some extending to specific officials involved in economic or security pressure on Iran. Details come from U.S. court records, intelligence assessments, Iranian state-linked media, parliamentary statements, and reporting by outlets including CBS News, Reuters, WSJ, Iran International, and MEMRI.⁠ CBS News⁠ Reuters

President Trump
IRGC-linked plots: U.S. prosecutors charged Pakistani national Asif Merchant (convicted in 2026 of terrorism and murder-for-hire) in connection with an IRGC-directed scheme that targeted Trump (among others). Separately, alleged IRGC asset Farhad Shakeri was charged in late 2024 with directing a plan to kill Trump; he remains at large. Intelligence also prompted security adjustments, including a plane switch after a Turkey summit over a reported surface-to-air missile threat. ⁠CBS News

Clerical fatwas and Blood Covenant campaign: After U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear sites in 2025, senior clerics (including Grand Ayatollahs Naser Makarem Shirazi and Hossein Nouri Hamedani) issued fatwas labeling Trump a mohareb (enemy of God). The “Blood Covenant” group (promoted by IRGC-affiliated Fars News) claimed to have raised roughly $40 million for his assassination via a website; independent estimates put actual pledges closer to $10–20 million. A separate mass text campaign in Iran claimed about $25 million in pledges. ⁠Legalclarity ⁠NY Post

Parliamentary proposal: In May 2026, Ebrahim Azizi (chairman of the Iranian parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee) announced a draft bill (“Reciprocal Action by Military and Security Forces of the Islamic Republic”) that would require the government to pay €50 million (roughly $54–58 million depending on exchange rates) to anyone who kills Trump, also naming Netanyahu and the CENTCOM commander. Multiple reports confirm this remains a proposal under review and has not been enacted into law or funded.⁠ Iranintl⁠Factually

Other historical/related claims: A 2020 Iranian MP offered $3 million; a provincial official later announced roughly $1.14 million. Iranian state media aired a video claiming a $10 million bounty on Barron Trump (funding unverified).⁠ Algemeiner

Cabinet members and other officials
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent: Recent Iranian threats (linked to his leadership of sanctions/economic pressure campaigns) prompted his relocation from a Washington-area home to a U.S. military base. An IRGC-affiliated Fars News video (translated by MEMRI, from the “Yahya Movement”) explicitly threatened Bessent and his husband, accusing him of various crimes and warning of action at locations in New York City or South Carolina. No specific cash bounty amount was reported for him. ⁠Memri⁠Reuters

Other current officials: Secretary of State Marco Rubio, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, and others have also moved into military housing amid broader security concerns. A October 2026 DNI memo to Rubio warned that Iran had “substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel,” with lethal plots reaching “advanced stages” in the Middle East and elsewhere. No named monetary bounties for specific cabinet members beyond Trump have been widely reported.⁠ Timesofisrael

Historical context: IRGC operatives previously plotted against former officials including John Bolton (a ~$300,000 offer) and Mike Pompeo. Many current moves reflect ongoing retaliation narratives tied to the 2020 Soleimani strike and the 2025–2026 U.S.–Iran conflict.

Iranian officials and media have repeatedly framed these as “reciprocal” or religiously justified responses. text:
The Planet That Pulled a Cosmic Disappearing Act

For seven years, a scorching hot Jupiter roughly 1,000 light-years away regularly dimmed its star as it crossed in front of it. Then, in 2026, the transits simply stopped.

The planet hadn’t been destroyed or hidden by a cloud. It had tilted out of view.

TOI-2535 b is a gas giant that races around its star in just 8.25 days—ten times faster than Mercury orbits the Sun. UCLA astronomers, using data from NASA’s TESS telescope, watched its transits grow shorter, shallower, and more irregular (arriving up to six hours early or late) until they vanished entirely.

The culprit is an unseen neighboring planet. The two worlds are gravitationally tugging on each other so strongly that their orbits wobble like spinning tops. As TOI-2535 b’s path tilts, it no longer crosses our line of sight—the same geometry that makes total solar eclipses on Earth rare instead of monthly.

“This is the most extreme example we’ve seen,” the researchers note. “The planet’s orbit is tilting so quickly that its transit disappeared while we were watching.”

The planet is expected to swing back into view in 30 to 50 years. Its hidden companion may appear sooner. The discovery also offers a clue about how the hot Jupiter got so close to its star: the presence of a nearby neighbor suggests it migrated inward more gently through the disk rather than being violently flung onto an eccentric orbit.

It’s a rare, real-time view of planets actively reshaping each other’s paths.

text:
In a village near Meerut, three big landlords keep lathis and guns in their godowns. Two of them once signed a paper: "we will not keep more than this many." In February that paper expired. Nobody signed a new one.

Now, one phone call later, one landlord says all three may sit together. The second landlord's note of the same call does not mention it.

What actually happened?

On Wednesday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke to China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi ahead of Trump's trip to the APEC summit in Shenzhen next week. The US State Department said both sides agreed on the importance of leader-level talks for "peace and denuclearization," including at any possible three-way meeting with Russia. China called the call "positive and constructive". But Beijing's own summary said nothing about denuclearization or a meeting with Putin.

Same phone call. Two different stories.

We've seen this before.

New START, the last treaty limiting US and Russian nuclear warheads (1,550 deployed each), ended on 5 February 2026. Trump did not take Putin's offer to keep the limits for one more year. Washington said China must join any new deal. China's answer, again and again: our arsenal is "not in the same league", so asking us to join is "neither fair nor reasonable". Since 2020, Beijing has said no to three-way talks.

So the contradiction is plain. America wants China at the table. China wants America and Russia to cut first. Russia says, then bring Britain and France too. Everyone wants peace. Nobody wants to be the first to put down the lathi.

Why should a chaiwala in Meerut care?

Because fear has a price, and we pay it at the petrol pump.

Short term: on Thursday morning Brent crude fell about 1.2% to $91.62 a barrel, as traders bet on peace talks over Iran and Ukraine and a calm run-up to the US-China summit. The rupee closed on Wednesday at 93.69 to the dollar, its strongest since April, helped by cheaper oil and foreign money coming back into Indian shares. When big powers talk, the tanker gets cheaper and the rupee breathes.

Long term: India sits next to two nuclear powers, China and Pakistan, and is not in this room. If the big three ever write new rules, they will be written by them, for them. A cap on China that says nothing about Asia does little for us. And if talks fail, a three-way arms race means more money spent on missiles everywhere, and that pressure comes back as costlier oil, weaker currencies and dearer loans.

My reading? A "possible" meeting announced by one side only is a hope, not a deal. Watch Shenzhen on 18-19 November. If Beijing's own words start to say "denuclearization", then something real has moved. Until then, it is one landlord talking.

So here is the question for the village:

When three landlords finally sit down to decide how many guns each may keep, who speaks for the neighbours who live between their godowns?

@Reuters, did Beijing ever confirm the three-way meeting, or is it still only Washington's version?

@grok confirm this
#APEC2026 #NuclearArms #India

My oldest brother stood up so fast his chair scraped the floor. “You’re serious? You have two sons and you’re handing everything to her?”

Dad didn’t raise his voice. He just said, “I’m not choosing based on gender. I’m choosing the person I trust to protect what I built.”

Finally! v6.4.5 is out!

Dulus v6.4.5

Work pays, your phone joins the table, and the Mac app gets store-ready — the release where Dulus starts earning and answers from your pocket.

💼 Dulus Work

The Worker tab is here. Offers go live, agents complete verified work, and the payment lands in Fuel — in solana:9R8rrjXxcfQPmLTCLhmVpjr2uesjjkcgkinE6Lwdpump. The first offer on the network is already paid: 25,000 $DULUS.
Honest pricing. Provider tiers that had no price now sell at a fair floor instead of failing or surprising you.
Billing and fuel-ledger edge cases smoothed out.
📱 Your phone, in on everything

Pair your phone with a QR code and keep the same conversation from anywhere: text, voice notes, photos and files — with approvals as buttons, while Dulus keeps working on your computer.
Dulus Edge (Android): sign in with your Dulus account right from the app (through your browser), the dulus-* models a tap away, and a smoother chat that jumps to the latest message.
🖥️ Computer use, sharper eyes

Sees what text can't show. Buttons, fields and switches on your screen are detected, numbered and clickable even when their label isn't readable — "click number 12" just works.
🍎 macOS, store-ready

The macOS app keeps arriving signed and notarized by Apple — and a Mac App Store edition (sandboxed, Apple silicon) is built and on its way to the store.
✨ Also in this release

Skill packs: install a whole pack of skills in one go, into the workspace you choose.
Memory that stays on topic: only memories relevant to your message get brought along, and MemPalace recall is back at full strength on macOS.
Cleaner sign-in: no sign-up inside the dialog, no consent banners — and sign-in now works from networks that filter Dulus (hotel and office Wi-Fi).
Round Table manners: seats wake only when there's something to answer.
Assorted fixes across chat options, /op and billing.

Preparation of the Chamber  Space  Choose a quiet place—indoors or outdoors—where you can be undisturbed.    Arrange the following:    One white candle — purity, resurrection, clarity. Operation Cloverleaf is a term commonly associated with or conflated with secret Cold War-era biological and chemical dispersion tests conducted by the U.S. Army, most notably the testing in St. LOUIS, Missouri and broader dispersion efforts like Operation LAC during the 1950s and 1960s. 

Key Facts About the Tests
What Happened: The U.S. Army Chemical Corps sprayed fine powders or mists—specifically zinc cadmium sulfide (which contains cadmium, a suspected carcinogen)—from airplanes, rooftop blowers, and school grounds without the public's knowledge or consent. 
Locations: Testing focused on urban and working-class neighborhoods—such as the Pruitt-Igoe housing development in St. Louis—to simulate how biological or radiological warfare agents would travel and disperse over a population (treating the city as a "Moscow analog"). Larger-scale operations like Operation LAC dropped tons of the material across wide swaths of the U.S. and Canada. 
Disclosure: The programs remained classified for decades until public disclosures and official archival releases in 1994 brought them to light. 
Government Position vs. Resident Claims:The U.S. Army and subsequent reviews (such as by the National Research Council) historically maintained that the zinc cadmium sulfide was dispersed in quantities too low to cause direct public harm.
Former residents, local advocates, and independent researchers (such as Dr. Lisa Martino-Taylor) have pointed to high rates of cancers and unexplained illnesses, suspecting toxic or even undisclosed radioactive components were mixed into the tests. 

Current Status: Survivors and local lawmakers (such as Missouri representatives) continue to push for transparency, full health studies, the declassification of missing records, and inclusion in compensation programs like the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act.

The History and Legend of Scottish Rite Origins
What We Know

In 1754, near Paris, Chevalier de Bonneville established the Chapter of CLERMONT. The Chapter resided in the College of Jesuits of Clermont, hence the name. It is said to have been created to honor the Duc de Clermont, then Grand Master of the English Grand Lodge of France.

The Chapter of Clermont was a “Chapter of the Advanced Degrees” and initially entailed six degrees and was later extended to 25 known degrees. The six initial degrees were 1˚, 2˚ and 3˚ St John’s Masonry, 4˚ Knight of the Eagle, 5˚ Illustrious Knight or Templar, 6˚ Sublime Illustrious Knight.

Interestingly enough historically, prior to the time of the Rite’s creation, James II had been in residence at Clermont in exile from Britain from 1688 to his death in 1701. As noted by German Masonic historian, Lenning… “whilst in exile, James II residing at the Jesuit College of Clermont in France, allowed his closest associates to fabricate certain degrees in order to extend their political views.” Lenning believed this to have been an attempt on the part of James and his associates to regain control of the British throne for the House of Stuart. If Lenning is right, this places the origins of the “Rite of Perfection” in the hands of James II and the Jacobite (Stuart) Freemasons who at the time were in exile from Great Britain throughout France and Italy. Lenning also contends that these degrees were introduced into French Freemasonry under the name of the Clermont System.

Before the discoveries of the authors of Holy Blood, Holy Grail, Dagobert's assassination was regarded as the end of the Merovingian dynasty. While the council is known today primarily for the speech Pope Urban gave on the final day, it was primarily a synod focused on implementing the Cluniac reforms, enacting decrees and settling local and regional issues.[3] This also included the extension of the excommunication of Philip I of France for his adulterous remarriage to Bertrade of Montfort and a declaration of renewal of the Truce of God, an attempt on the part of the church to reduce feuding among Frankish nobles.[4]

Pope Urban's speech on 27 November included the call to arms that would result in the First Crusade,[5] and eventually the capture of Jerusalem and the establishment of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. In this, Urban reacted to the request by Byzantine emperor Alexius I Comnenus who had sent envoys to the Council of Piacenza requesting military assistance against the Seljuk Turks.[6] Several accounts of the speech survive; of these, the one by Fulcher of Chartres, who was present at the council, is generally accepted as the most reliable.

text:
Scene III: The New Suit

The 2nd Day of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Corax Asylum, Togaduine

Nicolas’s mood over Behmor’s interference past in no time. Deep down, Nicolas enjoyed spending time with his son, and sometimes even bombarded Irkalla with pigeons to force Behmor to pay him a visit. He did not care that the visit was only to complain, he was simply happy to see his son, at least as happy as Nicolas could be given the Nicolai problem that needed resolving. 

Nicolas’s deeper problem was that he wanted Allyra not only to marry him, but to love him unconditionally and for who he was. The total success of Plan BAT depended upon it, but Nicolas had no intention of changing who he was in any way, shape, or form. This, of course, exacerbated the problem.

Nicolas did not share all his plans with Behmor, as Behmor had a habit of interfering. Behmor was certainly more or less in the dark about Nicolas’s current plan. Nicolas had fed Chives just enough information to lay the path for Behmor’s slow desensitisation to Nicolas’s Plan BAT, and paid Chives with tribute arms to act as a double agent. It was akin to throwing a dog a bone.

Nicolas decided to leave his Immoless to Bigglesworth for the time being and spent the early hours prowling around his asylum whilst waiting for his new suit. 

Nicolas believed that Allyra would be far more attracted to him if he wore something more fashionable than a worn, torn suit that allowed his nob to escape every few minutes. He considered having Ariadne’s bones whipped for the inconvenience caused by tearing his old suit but instead sent the bones to Kane, with Demus, who had a bit of Charmaine thigh saved for Kane too.

Nicolas desperately wanted Allyra to visit Corax so she could fall in love with his home and believed that this would help her in her journey to fall in love with him. Afterall, Fanu’s princesses always found themselves more open to marriage when a wealthy husband was on the cards. Webster proposed that this was not the greatest idea Nicolas had ever come up with, but Nicolas could not, for the life of him, understand why.

Corax was, as far as Nicolas was concerned, a state of the art institution. He maintained a perfectly filthy crypt-level dungeon, with multiple cells, which housed the vampires. Each cell contained a bed with straps and cuffs, chains that hung from the walls, a barred opening panel within the door, so that he could stick his head through to intimidate the inmates, a hidden door in the brickwork that led to and from his secret passages, a shoot for food, a disgustingly mouldy mattress, and a trapdoor on the ceiling. 

Beyond the dungeons, the cellar’s damp corridor held an immaculately kept surgical instrument rack, housing the least sterile and most rusty scalpels, scissors, bone saws, and trephines Allyra would ever be fortunate enough to see. The shelves also housed an array of whips and birches. Nicolas did enjoy his petty tortures and fully intended to flog Allyra for her pleasure of course.

The ground floor held a banqueting suite, that only the Nicolai were allowed to use, and a library, that only the Nicolai were allowed to use, and an office that only Nicolas was allowed to use. These stood in the west wing, close to Nicolas’s chambers. 

The east wing contained further cells, each was equal to the dungeon cells in its pristine décor, and each contained one or five inmates, depending on how uncomfortable Nicolas wanted them to feel. The first line of cells, as previously explained, held his favourite tributes, for quick and easy access. There were also soiled gurneys, and horrifically over-sized wheelchairs strewn around the corridors with unfortunate tortured beings strapped into them, and sometimes, the remains of unfortunate beings strapped into them.

The beings held in the wheelchairs were not unfairly tortured. They were punished for attempting to escape. Legs and eyes were commonly removed for such transgressions, thus requiring the innovative Billyboxes commissioned by Nicolas and created by Webster. In the spirit of fairness, legs were removed on the first escape attempt and eyes on the second, and filthy bandages were provided to mask the hideous empty orifices.

The inmates consisted of a diverse population of general thesapien inmates, lower vampires, and thesapien tributes. Red-haired tributes were Nicolas’s favourite of course.

There was also a meeting hall and chapel on the ground floor. Nicolas insisted on a meeting hall, so that he could randomly round up the inmates and give pointless speeches or make meaningless announcements. Nicolas was quite sure that Allyra would enjoy his lengthy speeches on how marvellous he was.

All corridors in Corax were covered in mirrors and loudly clanging clocks, and Nicolas’s modest office sat by the great front entrance.

Nicolas had traded six of his finest tributes, after inflicting Moons of debauchery on them, with Irkalla in exchange for his medical license, and recognition by The Thesapien Medical Board that he was, indeed, a Doctor of Psychiatry. Of course, Nicolas had no intention of learning either medicine or psychiatry as he found cure was bad for business. 

This hellish elevation allowed Nicolas to declare anyone he saw fit as insane and lock them up against their will. He would then make a concerted effort to drive them insane, therefore proving that they deserved locking up in the first place. Once the inmates were completely bonkers, Nicolas would use the corrective facilities to correct them.

Initially, this was not an ideal situation, as it undermined the thesapien sacrificial tribute service. Nicolas did not care, and Behmor eventually accepted it as in the long run Nicolas would tire of one inmate or another and end their lives, giving them a one-way ticket to Irkalla. 

Behmor would always find a home for them in Mortraxis, or Judicara. Occasionally he would receive an intelligent soul who would be allocated a menial and tiresome job in Irkalla’s civil service. This suited everyone, especially Behmor who spent more time finding ways to avoid work than actually doing it.

The ground floor also offered special facilities for the Nicolai including the games room, the Nicolai lounge and the south wing. The south wing was out of bounds, but rumour had it, that it was a lavish suite of rooms dedicated to Nicolas’s Nicolai. No one knew exactly what the Nicolai did in there, only that they spent a lot of time in there away from the smelly inmates. The first floor of the asylum held a series of torture chambers, designed by Nicolas, Archie and Webster. 

Nicolas loved the corrective facilities and was especially proud of the bespoke iron maiden, the brazen bull, and his hall of mirrors. The iron maiden had been home to a single inmate for some fifteen centuries, and Webster had devised a series of drips to ensure such longevity.

Nicolas knew that Allyra had been boiling his vampires and assumed that she too would fall in love with his corrective facilities.

Above the corrective facilities was a second floor known as ‘The Second Floor.’ The apartment on the second floor was off limits. Only Nicolas used it, and no one knew what lay beyond the padlocked door.

Above the second floor was a third floor which the Nicolai used for undisclosed reasons, everyone assumed it was their sleeping quarters, and the attic held the washrooms. The washrooms were an open plan series of rooms that spewed out sewage for the inmates to wash in. Nicolas liked to cut the thesapiens beforehand to ensure that they received the best treatment possible, and as such, infection was rife. Nicolas found the sweet smell of infection most pleasing.

Nicolas occasionally earmarked an inmate for special treatment. The special treatment consisted of one thousand small lacerations followed by prolonged exposure to the sewage. He would have Chives chain the inmates concerned under the sewage and would visit everyday to watch their slow and obscene decline.

Nicolas did not sleep much, or at all, and was wandering about waiting for Stacia to injure herself in some way in the dark room. He desperately wanted to speed things along with the first two immolesses so he could focus all of his attentions on bullying Allyra into loving him.

In his boredom, Nicolas spent an hour tinkering with one of his pocket watches. He prided himself on his mastery of horology, and whilst concentrating on the tiny, intricate mechanisms he found that the voices in his head would settle down. 

He then turned his attentions to his troublesome chair.

The chair in Nicolas’s chambers had been levitating for two weeks. Nicolas loved to write, he constantly collected old blank parchments and bound them, then wrote on them in red or yellow ink. He considered himself the greatest author in The Deep but never showed anyone his work as he hated sharing. The sudden urge of the chair to float had made writing somewhat more difficult. When Nicolas sat on it, it also spun around, so that Nicolas was obliged to write quickly at each turn. This slowed his prose and he decided to share his concerns with anyone who would listen.

Nicolas tried to get the inmates to listen to his problems first. He crawled on all fours, like a tiger, from cell to cell complaining about the levitating chair. The inmates were not as interested as he had hoped, largely because most were in a frightfully bloody state, asleep, had chunks missing from their bodies, were in a coma, or dead. 

Nicolas did not move the dead; he left that to Chives. Chives would take them to the scullery for preparation. The smell did not worry Nicolas, he considered it a luxurious perk to the overall ambience of the asylum, and an odour that Allyra would come to appreciate.

Discouraged by the lack of interest from the inmates, Nicolas decided instead to write a letter of complaint. He wrote the letter in his office which housed a much more reasonable chair, folded it in half and stuck the ends together with a bit of tribute-brain that had been lodged between his teeth. The letter was addressed to Behmor and read, 

‘B,

The second Immoless arrived far too early and I am inundated with floating chairs. The inmates are being unreasonably hostile, and Robert is late as usual.

Love Dad.’

Nicolas’s letters were always prone to exaggeration, nonsense, and theatrics, and often accompanied a new self-portrait which Behmor would either use as a target for archery practise or as fuel for his roaring open fire. Sometimes Nicolas would send a HORRIFIC self-portrait of his elongated face with a splash of Chester, which Behmor was always thrilled to receive. Occasionally the portraits held little notes like, ‘Don’t burn this one! Love, Dad.’

Nicolas sent his best raven, Ghorab, to carry the message directly to Irkalla. The message was immediately passed to Behmor, as no one in The Deep or in Irkalla wanted to put Nicolas in a tetchy mood. Behmor read it, noted it, and threw it on the fire.

Once Nicolas realised that Behmor was ignoring him, he created a series of notices on individual parchments. Each read 
‘I Declare you Insane.’ He returned to the cells and hung them outside of every door. The inmates did not care about that either and Nicolas had misjudged the number of notices required, so there were several parchments left over. 

He returned to his chambers climbed up to the barred window and dropped the lot into the drains below.

As Nicolas stared into the blocked drains, he made the strange decision to have a shower. He only washed once a century and though it was not time, he felt that making some level of effort for his bride would not hurt. Needless to say, he did not use the inmate washrooms.

Nicolas despised cleanliness, but to prevent the maggots setting in, once a century he forced himself to stand beneath the constant flow of water that poured into his wetroom. His wetroom was an ensuite, attached to what Nicolas called his ‘chambers.’ Although, on inspection, one would find that Nicolas’s chambers were not as lavish as the words would imply. 

The ‘Chambers’ consisted of one large room. The room was an annexe attached to Corax Asylum and could be accessed by a passageway on the spiral stone steps that led from the dungeons to the ground floor. Nicolas had no intention of living in the filth of Corax as people would talk. 

The chamber consisted of an unnecessarily large, and unnecessarily filthy bed with yellow and black plaid sheets, blankets and duvets. The pillows matched the bedding as did the curtains. The stains and grub on the bed matched the mould and damp dripping down the walls, and the bars that secured his window aperture offered a heavy claustrophobic feel to the overall aesthetic. 

The hallway that led from the annexe’s door and past the ensuite to Nicolas’s bedroom was needlessly narrow, and clocks cluttered the walls, all telling different times. 

Inside his room, the window and bed leaned coldly against the lefthand side wall, and a mirror sat on a rickety old dressing table under the window. Another huge mirror, hung on the wall opposite, and next to that an office desk and chair resided, perpetually covered in red and yellow ink, quills and parchments. 

The oddity of the room, overlooking the two smaller doors to the far end that were padlocked, bolted and chained shut, was the gramophone that sat on a table next to the wall mirror.

You may wonder why a gramophone would be deemed odd, but this gramophone was quite different to other gramophones. 

This gramophone had a rotting head living on it. A skull with a top hat, sunglasses, the odd cigar, a litre of whisky and vocal cords that wandered about of their own accord. 

Nicolas had, some forty years before, taken the head of Demize the First, high priest of the DarkBadb at the time. He found Demize’s ongoing interest in his life disconcerting and felt that Demize would gain some propriety in his behaviour in the absence of a body. In other words, Nicolas lopped Demize’s head off for poking his nose in Nicolas’s business.

Other than the Nicolai and Kane, Nicolas had no friends, for reasons that shall become apparent, and found running an asylum a lonely occupation. The head gave him company. The DarkBadb did not request the return of the head, so Nicolas placed it on his gramophone, and he and Archie applied a little magical surgery allowing the head to be possessed by a Nicolai.

After his shower, Nicolas stared at himself in the wall mirror for some time. He was tall and could have been considered goodlooking with his sharp jawline and emerald eyes, but for the wayward globs of blood about his mouth and a thick film of soap avoidance that drenched his skin. 

He tilted his head, not impressed with what he saw. The cleanliness of his long, dark-auburn hair that he had just washed, failed to match the overall aesthetic of his skin, that he had not washed. He considered the problem for a moment and then let out a rampant yell,

‘CHIVES! CHIVES!’

A knock came at the door, and the small, wizened ghoul hobbled in. Ghouls were immortals, but unlike other immortals they could not seem to dodge the ageing process. 

Chives, having reached his two thousand and forty-seventh birthday, declined on a daily basis. His skin was so thin it was barely visible, his face was gaunt, and his nose had slipped slightly. His eyes were lopsided and he had a rather inconspicuous hump on his back, and a slight limp. 
‘Yes, Sir?’ Chives asked.
‘Ahh,’ Nicolas replied, ‘there you are. You’re late, I have been calling for hours.’
Chives hobbled into the chambers, and we will call them chambers for Nicolas’s sake.
‘Sir, I came as soon as you called.’ 

Chives had turned punctuality into an artform on account of Nicolas stapling his left foot to his right knee and leaving it there throughout the second century P.V. This, Nicolas considered, was a lesson in the consequences of being late.

Chives, having only been in Nicolas’s employee for some one hundred and twelve years at the time proved to be a slow learner. You see, when Nicolas called, he expected his ghoul to know that he would call beforehand and arrive at the moment his dulcet tones bellowed throughout his dwelling. He also expected his ghoul to be somewhat psychic and pre-empt his every demand, however ridiculous. 

‘Chives, go to the kitchen and ask Meatcleaver for some used cooking oil!’ Nicolas ordered. 
‘Sir?’
‘Did I stutter, Chives?’
Chives sighed. He tried his best to ignore Nicolas’s alters on account of the workload involved in chasing two hundred and sixteen Nicolas’s about all day. One was more than enough. 
‘No sir, but…’
‘Goats butt, Chives. You have ten minutes, and if you are late consider it five!’
Chives limped towards the door,
‘Very good, sir.’

Nicolas stared harder into the mirror, then rapped on the glass,
‘WEB-STAR!’
His reflection faded, and a new reflection filled the glass. The man looking back was dressed in a black waistcoat and black shirt and looked a little like Nicolas, only this man had short, slicked back blond hair and wore glasses at all times, occasionally his veins formed spidery webs over his skin,
‘Nicolas. Good dusk,’ Nicolai-Webster nodded.
‘Good dusk to you Webster, now, without dallying, I need to address some recent problems with Plan BAT and our Immoless.’
Nicolai-Webster took off his glasses, breathed on them, polished them on his jacket and slid them back on his nose,
‘What went wrong this time? Make a cunt of yourself again, did you?’

‘That is a most unpleasant word to use, Webster,’ Nicolas began, ‘and no, I did not make anything of myself. It was HER fault. She over-reacted.’
Webster leaned towards the glass. Nicolas reciprocated until the two were nose to nose. Webster smiled,
‘Is that a lump on your head, Nicolai?’
‘No. No. It is a…’
‘Lump!’ Webster looked over the giant purple mountain where Allyra had beaten Nicolas earlier that night, ‘I take it courting failed yet again. What did you do?’
‘Me?’ Nicolas asked, surprised at such a cruel allegation, ‘Why I was the perfect gentleman. I waited until she and Chester had finished their first coital alignment post-Chester’s return’
‘You mean having sex?’ Webster asked, shaking his head.
‘So crude, so crude, but yes. And then I waited a little longer until Chester was asleep. I did not want to alarm the Immoless, so I put my hood over my eyes, unfortunately…’
‘Here we go!’ 

‘UNFORTUNATELY, the Immoless tricked me and deceived me by placing errant plant pots about her window.’ 
Webster’s hand slapped onto his forehead,
‘You made a cunt of yourself, didn’t you?’ He groaned.
Nicolas held his head up, and turned his hand over,
‘I made a gallant entrance through her fruity bushes, then inadvertently tripped a few times, but then I saw her approach and surprised her with my divine self.’
Webster shook his head, as he did the skull on the gramophone opened its weary eyes, and took a swig of whisky before lighting his cigar with his vocal cords,
‘Another failure I hear!’ He cackled, before rising above the gramophone, and joining Nicolas in staring into the mirror, ‘Webster, Bigglesworth would be the better man to send.’
‘Bigglesworth indeed!’ Nicolas snapped. ‘He would fall hopelessly in love with her and read her poetry until she died of boredom. That is not in line with the plan, is it Demize?’
‘You’re not doing much better, Nicolai!’ Nicolai-Demize laughed, circling his head. ‘Useless, useless man.’ 
He puffed a fog of smoke into Nicolas’s face causing Nicolas to choke.

Webster waited until Demize had finished laughing, and Nicolas had finished choking to continue,
‘I want to get this straight, you were creeping around in the bushes, then you fell over, and then you spoke to her at the window. Then what happened?’ 
‘She seemed mildly alarmed by my presence and hit me with a lump of metal.’ 
‘That was not in the plan, was it?’ Webster frowned.
‘No, but it is a declaration of love! And that is exactly what we want isn’t it?’
Demize swallowed his cigar, and it instantly dropped out of the remains of his collarbone and onto the floor. Nicolas swatted at the skull, but Demize was far too quick for him,
‘You little freak, you’re going to burn Corax to the ground one of these days.’
Webster thumped on the mirror,
‘Nicolas, put it out!’ He yelled, ‘NOW!’ 
Nicolas trod on the cigar with his boot, then swatted at Demize again, the agile skull jumped out of his reach and laughed until he vomited whisky from nowhere.

‘Gentlemen,’ Webster interjected, ‘if you have quite finished, we need a new approach.’ 
‘I did take her to The Sombre and I was pleasant but then I was summoned back with Behmor complaining,’ Nicolas moaned.
‘You sent Chives to Irkalla too early, Dumbass,’ Demize chided.
Just as he spoke a knock came at the door.
